facts.notes: Year of the figures not stated; pages updated Aug–Sep 2026.

facts.value: Lund University example: food SEK 3,000 + accommodation 4,000–8,000 + books 400–1,000 + misc 1,500 = about SEK 8,900–13,500/month (transport not itemised).
facts.notes: Total is the sum of the university's items, computed by us; the page gives no year.

facts.value: Monthly pass about SEK 634 regular (Numbeo, Nov 2026); students get 25% off ordinary Skånetrafiken tickets with a student ID app.
facts.notes: Official Skånetrafiken 30-day price for Lund not found on the page read.

facts.value: Mean temperature about 0.9 °C in January and 18.3 °C in July; about 676 mm precipitation/year (SMHI 1991–2020).
facts.notes: Wikipedia climate table citing SMHI 1991–2020 normals; SMHI's own tables were not reached.

facts.value: Student life centres on the 13 student nations (clubs, sports, parties); student unions also organise social activities.
English is enough for daily life, but typical student jobs (shops, cafés) generally require some Swedish.
Competitive: 46,000+ students compete for part-time work; the university rarely hires bachelor's/master's students. International firms, science parks and start-ups nearby.
No city data. National example: hotel/restaurant agreement floor SEK 153.64–164.30/hour (from 1 Apr 2026, no experience; youth rates under 20). No statutory minimum wage.
facts.source_name: HRF (Hotel and Restaurant Workers' Union) – Gröna Riksavtalet
facts.notes: A collective-agreement wage floor for one sector, not a measured typical student wage; no citable source for typical student pay found.
